chapter: Brawls, the Ink Spots and boyhood recollections
title: Wishing he had finished school; thieves and liars
summary: He admits he left business details to others and wishes he had finished school, then complains about educated crooks and a Southern president.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Well, I guess you never took a very active role in the business part of your career. You always let somebody else handle that and very often you didn't find out the details. You pretty much just went along with the business as it was presented to you.
And you're saying now if you had learned more about the business you would have been further -- as far

I went to the bottom. That's all right -- top and bottom, okay? Now, you see, I would rather have finished school and learned what was needed more so than I wound up in this. I wisht I hadda finished school because I would have had more brains on the world than I have, in all these crises, I'd have been one of them guys up there on that there calendar,man. I would have been one of them guys, you know that? Because I know I've got the mind -- those are the presidents. And to think what education you have to have. Of course you don't need no education to be a thief and a liar. You don't need that for that. And that's what we've turned out to have. Men finish school and turn out to be thieves and liars. That's all they turned out to be. A bunch of crooks. And why they do that, I don't know. That's what it's

turned out to be.
And how they could have
reached down south to get a man for President
and leave a person that's more deserving of
being in a position for . . .
